A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. All appendix content is retained; pagination and figure relocation do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–7 and Appendix A report original OGBench experiments on policy performance, robustness, feature plasticity, and high-UTD online reinforcement learning.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Sections 4–7 and Appendix A, including performance comparisons and controlled interventions.

M1.justification: The flow-matching critic, expected-value TD objective in Equations 3–4, integration procedure, and RLPD adaptations in Section 7 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OGBench single-task environments for offline analyses and online learning with prior data. No evaluated task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same distributional floq variant and monolithic FQL comparisons, including ResNet and transformer critics. The TQL comparison in footnote 1 is also retained.

E3.justification: Experimental settings remain identical, including the 250,000-step staleness checkpoint, feature freezing at 0.5M steps, target-noise levels, BC coefficient tuning, and UTD sweeps in Sections 5–7 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: The staleness, noisy-target, feature-norm, feature-freezing, single-integration-step, and velocity-versus-final-target analyses are retained. Appendix A adds no new analyses relative to v1.

E5.justification: Figures 7 and 11 retain standard-deviation shading across random seeds. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty procedures, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains hmmaze-large success rates of 52% versus 30% for expected-value versus distributional floq. Figure 7 is relocated without changing its results.

T1.justification: Definitions 5.1–5.2, Theorem 6.1, and the assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions attribute the benefits to test-time recovery and feature plasticity rather than distributional RL. The claims of roughly 2× final performance and 5× sample efficiency in high-UTD settings are retained.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the humanoidmaze-medium staleness exception, assumptions underlying recovery guarantees, and the proposed extension beyond linear theoretical analysis.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page link explicitly identifying code and runs. The acknowledgments also specify the ACCESS allocation for already acknowledged NCSA Delta resources. Implementation descriptions and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not verify the linked artifacts.

R1.justification: The same 60 references and substantive research positioning are retained. The new resource link and expanded funding acknowledgment do not revise relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: V2 adds the code-and-runs sentence and expands the NCSA/ACCESS acknowledgment, alongside the version/date update. Scientific prose and section ordering are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 moves from page 14 within Section 7 in v1 to a standalone page 21 after the references in v2. Text and footnotes reflow, but figure designs, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new first-page code-and-runs pointer modestly improves resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation, although artifact completeness cannot be established from the PDFs. Scientific content and appendices are unchanged. Moving Figure 7 away from its discussion slightly worsens navigation, limiting the overall benefit.
